newsitem.title: FRANCE: France calls off CIC bank privatisation.
newsitem.headline: France calls off CIC bank privatisation.

text.p: France called off the sale of big regional banking group CIC on Thursday and blamed the heads of the bank and its state-owned parent insurer GAN for failing to help with the privatisation.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announced the cancellation of a sell-off tender launched in August, which drew offers from BNP and Societe Generale, but said that he was determined that the CIC group would be sold off eventually.
"After serious reflection the government has decided to call off the privatisation process for CIC," Arthuis said.

"It seemed important that everyone had the necessary time for reflection," he told a news conference on the sale of 67 percent of CIC shares with a book value of about 9.4 billion francs ($1.85 billion).
"The managers of GAN and CIC did not behave in a way to encourage progress in this process," Arthuis said.
He said he had decided to abandon the privatisation process in view of public and staff reactions to the sale but that the government remained determined to sell CIC in the future.
"There is no question of not privatising CIC," he said.
CIC, or Credit Industriel et Commercial, still needed to link up with a group capable of providing it with the funds it needed to develop, Arthuis said.

The privatisation tender launched in the summer carried a list of terms and conditions which suitors had to respect, including respect for CIC's regional integrity and insurance sales ties with parent Groupe des Assurances Nationales.

The tender was for sale of 67 percent of CIC, a profitable group of 11 regional banks whose main customers are medium and large companies and whose sell-off was seen as a prerequisite for the sale of GAN itself to the private sector later on.
Arthuis said France's independent privatisation commission had ruled that an offer by BNP complied with the government's terms and conditions but that it had rejected the offer from Societe Generale.
He said he had been concerned that there was only one offer on the table for CIC after the privatisation commission verdict.

CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt infuriated Arthuis in October after declaring on television at an extremely delicate stage in the privatisation tender that the bids could spell the "death" of his regional banking network.
Arthuis replied at the time: "It is unacceptable coming from a chairman and I shall draw the consequences".
French press said in the wake of the fracas that it was the intervention of GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud which avoided Yoncourt being fired.
Arthuis declined to comment on Thursday on whether Yoncourt would be replaced.

The privatisation of CIC had provoked strong resistance from staff who staged strikes to highlight their fears of job losses and a break-up of the regional banking group and it also raised concern among politicians. ($1=5.088 French Franc)
